items.title: For and against
items.content:
Early in my career, I was web performance and accessibility and building cool things.

But as JavaScript frameworks became increasingly ubiquitous, we saw the things I was start to degrade rapidly. Sites got slower and harder to use.

The web took on a boring sameness.

I spent increasing amounts of my time and energy being JS-heavy tooling like React and abstracting away writing code to NPM modules.

More recently, I’ve been AI. Like the JS libraries of yore, it’s making the web shittier… for the same reasons as JS frameworks, and many new reasons, too.

Friends, I’m so fucking sick of being things.

I want to be things again, but the current state of the web and the tech industry more broadly has made that relatively impossible for me when it comes to web developer topics.

That’s not to say there’s not still good things happening to the web. CSS is having a renaissance!

But the joy is gone .

They knew how. It wasn’t that they didn’t care or didn’t want to. They wanted. They still loved… what it had been.

But as they tried to connect to what had once been so captivating, they felt nothing but yawning absence. A void where they’d once been filled.

That’s essentially how I feel about dev more broadly right now.

I can do the work. I enjoy the rote feeling of wielding an experts tools to practice my craft. It’s meditative, when I get into the coding zone.

But that captivating spark? It’s gone.

I’m writing here a lot less lately because I’ve been finding meaning outside of the web.

I’ve been feeding people through a community farm stand I started out of my home. I’ve been doing outreach to unhoused folks in my area.

I’ve been talking to strangers and reading books and riding my bike and exploring the little nooks and crannies of the new town I call home now.

I should probably write more about those things.
